persona: Host and player trying to keep the room moving while listening
reasons: The installation photo proves that the actual bowl sat in an open steel cradle with an external spotlight, whereas the superseded proposal had enclosed glass, a velvet shelf and an internal lamp.

Minnie claims an internal-lamp job inside the alcove at 6:44 by the service clock. That job used nonexistent equipment, and the independently controlled curtain was already locked at 6:38. The ten-minute-fast brass clock does not excuse a service-clock claim.

Several others have the late impossible-time problem but describe real installed equipment. Other guests, including me, describe obsolete equipment during an earlier visit. Those alternatives prevent either contradiction alone from identifying the poisoner, but Minnie is the only person combining both.

Minnie acknowledges business around Grant’s salon before the invented alibi. The poisoned coupe was present there from 6:40, and linen/key access was shared. Her payment dispute gives a motive, though not a uniquely stronger motive than the others.
confusion: As an innocent player my own printed account is visibly false. Without a short private explanation that this is a cover for an unrelated scandal, I would worry my packet was wrong or my acting should change.

I have a complete replayable transcript here. A real host-player also handles envelopes, page turns and speaking order and may miss a crucial equipment or clock qualifier. This test does not establish comfortable human difficulty or timing.
repeated_or_giveaway_language: Multiple guests say exactly 'My other business that evening is not something I wanted Grant announcing over dinner.' The early fabricated accounts repeat 'Near the toast I was outside the enclosure ... dealing with my other business.' These repetitions reveal mechanical groupings.

The story still resolves through the one intersection of two contradictions. The new alternatives help, but after F4/F5 the comparison is straightforward for a listener who has preserved all statements.
Nobody explicitly confessed or accidentally read a guilty paragraph aloud in this scripted transcript. There is no observed live-player handling error to measure.
improvements: Vary the concealing explanations and sentence order; avoid identical phrasing marking whole suspect classes.
Explain privately that printed alibis can conceal an unrelated secret, and instruct players to stay with their printed answers until Coming Clean.
Let the room revisit evidence and request repeated answers before voting, especially because the host is also a player.

If a genuinely less deterministic mystery is desired, add a competing suspect with two apparent contradictions resolved by an independent contextual detail, so the final decision requires more than spotting the only double liar. Do not merely hide necessary evidence or make the innocent alternative unexplained.
Use a short human rehearsal to calibrate challenge and round duration; perfect-transcript model accuracy is a different measure.

protocol.assessment_type: Independent staged assessment of a scripted sixteen-character table; not a live interactive party
